INTRODUCTION

Phototransduction
in
vertebrate
retinal
rod
cells
involves
an
enzyme
cascade
in
which
the

second
messenger
cyclic
guanosine
monophosphate
( cGMP )
directly
controls
the
gating
of
cation

channels
in
the
cell
membrane
( Fensenko
et
al . ,
1985 )
to
regulate
the
photoreceptor
potential .
The

transduction
cascade
begins
when
light
isomerizes
the
chromophore
of
rhodopsin
( 11 - cis
retinal )

and
activates
the
GTP - binding
protein ,
transducin .
Activated
transducin
activates
cGMP

phosphodiesterase ,
which
lowers
the
concentration
of
cGMP
in

cell ,
leading
to
the
closing
of

cation
channels
and
hyperpolarization
of
the
photoreceptor
( Stryer ,
1986 ) .
